title: session-fenced-rehearsal-and-decision-tree-rollback-advisor
author: Sofia Ramos
release_notes: Adds a session-fenced rehearsal runner and decision-tree rollback advisor for safer staged model promotes. No customer-visible API changes; rollout controls enabled behind feature flag 'session_fence_rehearsal'.
body:
Problem and motivation: transient regressions during canary/promote phases can split user sessions (partial exposure) and produce noisy signals that confuse automated rollback heuristics. Operators asked for a way to rehearse staged promotes with session-coherent shadowing and a more explainable rollback decision path that considers sequence-level signals (session latency/semantic drift) in addition to aggregate metrics.

What this PR does: Implements a session-fenced rehearsal runner that replays a bounded history of a live session's requests into shadow lanes in sequence order, preserves KV-cache affinity for stateful models during rehearsal, and records per-session delta metrics. Adds a DecisionTree Rollback Advisor that consumes the rehearsal trace and online telemetry to produce an explainable rollback recommendation (allow/hold/rollback) with confidence scores and top contributing signals. Both features are gated behind the feature flag `session_fence_rehearsal` and a per-deployment config `session_fence_window_ms`.

Design highlights (continuous description): The rehearsal runner attaches to the existing shadow capture pipeline and batches per-session traces into replay buckets with sequence preservation and time-window bounds to avoid unbounded memory growth. To keep overhead predictable we use a sampling-first strategy: warm sessions are deterministically chosen by hash-based cohorting, cold sessions are sampled based on traffic fraction. The runner creates ephemeral rehearsal tasks that replicate network and KV cache interactions against the candidate model variant in a sandboxed runtime (no external side-effects). Rehearsal telemetry is emitted as a structured line: session_id, seq_index, latency_ms, token_delta, semantic_distance (embedding drift), error_flag, candidate_model, control_model. The DecisionTree advisor ingests aggregated rehearsal traces plus SLO metrics (p50/p95 latency, 5xx rate, embedding-population drift) and evaluates a small explainable tree (configurable weights) to return a verdict and the top 3 contributing signals.

Compatibility and safety: The sandboxed rehearsal uses the same runtime paths as production but with resource throttles and a separate cache namespace. There is no mutation to production state because we stub external services during rehearsal. The advisor is conservative by default (prefers hold over auto-rollback) and exposes an allowlist to enable auto-rollback for canaries marked as low-risk. We also added a dry-run telemetry mode so teams can exercise the advisor without impact.

Files and high-level changes: Implemented rehearsal runner service and scheduler: pkg/rollout/rehearsal_runner.go; DecisionTree advisor: pkg/rollout/rollback_advisor_tree.go; telemetry schemas and producers: internal/telemetry/rehearsal_schema.go; CLI controls and flags: cmd/rolloutctl/main.go, cmd/rolloutctl/commands/rehearse.go; unit and integration tests: test/rollout/rehearsal_test.go, test/rollout/advisor_integration_test.go; small runtime sandboxes and cache namespace wiring: runtime/sandbox.go, runtime/cache_namespace.go. Also updated docs: docs/rollouts/session_rehearsal.md and examples: examples/rehearsal-config.yaml.

Testing and verification: Added unit tests for sequence preservation, cache namespace isolation, and advisor decision boundaries. Integration tests run a simulated traffic harness (1000 sessions) that compares control vs candidate aggregated metrics and verifies advisor verdicts produce expected hold/allow/rollback outcomes under crafted regressions. CI flakiness observed in e2e in first run due to timing in sandbox cleanup; fixed by adding a deterministic cleanup signal. All CI checks passing on final run.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc attached and reviewed (ENG-4123) - [x] Feature gated behind 'session_fence_rehearsal' - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Telemetry schema reviewed by Observability - [x] Docs and example config - [x] Backwards-compatible and non-breaking by default

Migration notes: Operators can opt-in by enabling feature flag and setting `session_fence_window_ms` (default 5000). No database migrations required. Telemetry will start emitting rehearsal.* metrics; increase observability retention if teams want historical tracing.

Rollout plan: 1) Deploy to staging with feature flag enabled for internal fleets. 2) Run dry-run mode for 48 hours and validate advisor outputs vs manual audits. 3) Enable session-fenced rehearse on 10% of canaries and monitor telemetry dashboards added under rollout > session-rehearsal. 4) Gradually increase to 100% and consider enabling auto-rollback allowlist for low-risk services.

Related work: Builds on shadow-capture plumbing from ENG-3198 and complements the offline rehearsal harness from ENG-2680. Linear tickets ENG-4123 and ENG-4198 track follow-ups (tuning advisor weights, expanding signal set).

Summary of impact: Provides safer promotes for sessionful applications by preserving sequence context during rehearsal and giving operators an explainable advisor to reduce noisy auto-rollbacks and shorten MTTI for real regressions.
